sourceDiagnosis.rootCause: Chromium 143 aborts a keepalive fetch issued from pagehide when the document leaves via NAVIGATION (0/15 landed across headless+headed runs), but completes it normally when the TAB CLOSES (11/11 landed). A product-independent 17-byte keepalive control reproduced the identical split, exonerating the client flush implementation.
sourceDiagnosis.classification: BROWSER SEMANTICS, secondary TEST-MECHANISM DEFECT (the spec chose a discard shape whose guarantee Chromium does not offer).
sourceDiagnosis.commitDecisionInSourceDiagnosis: not committed there -- authored, gated, and proven 3x green, then reverted to HEAD pending orchestrator decision to apply.
sourceDiagnosis.specCitation: openspec/changes/design-campaign-authority-and-sync/specs/campaign-authority/spec.md:157-158 -- the client persistence layer SHALL make a bounded, BEST-EFFORT durable write on discard; the requirement obliges issuing the write, not guaranteeing the browser dispatches it.

diffSummary: Case (a) discards via page.close({ runBeforeUnload: true }) instead of page.goto('about:blank').
serverRecord() takes an APIRequestContext instead of a Page (case (a) reads the record after its page is closed); every other call site now passes page.request or the fixture's `request` explicitly.
Cold reload runs on a freshly opened page (context.newPage()) after context.addInitScript(() => localStorage.clear()), wrapped in its own withGate call.

expect(puts).toHaveLength(1) removed from case (a); the file documents why in a comment above the test: a request issued as the page closes is not reported to Playwright at page or context level (measured), so the count cannot be taken there -- the jsdom suite owns the exactly-once-write claim against a mocked fetch. expect(puts).toHaveLength(0) BEFORE the discard is kept, still proving the debounce had not fired.
RED ARM moved to the SAME discard shape (page.close) so the pair keeps discriminating -- a red arm on a different discard would only prove that other shape loses the mutation.

File header LIMIT paragraph and a new comment block above the test record the measured Chromium finding (navigation 0/15, close 11/11, bare-keepalive control 0/3 vs 3/3) so a future reader does not revert this to a navigation discard.
patch.whatStillDiscriminates: The revision assertion (before.version + 1, exact) and the red arm's zero-movement checks (version unchanged, currentDate unchanged, puts.toHaveLength(0)) still fail without the two campaignPersistenceWiring listeners -- confirmed by the RED ARM test passing in the same run.

nonClaims: The navigation-discard loss remains. A user who navigates away from the app (address bar, external link, back out of the SPA) still loses up to the 2 s debounce window of mutations on this Chromium. Tab close, window close, and in-app SPA route changes (which discard no document) are covered.
No product code was changed. The client's flush behavior is unchanged; only the test's discard mechanism and its assertions were corrected to match what Chromium actually guarantees.

No openspec file was edited and no task checkbox was flipped by this action, per instruction. The diagnosis's `proposedBoundedSlice` step 2 (widening task 1.6's NON-CLAIMS in design-campaign-authority-and-sync/tasks.md) was NOT performed here -- that remains an open item for the owner/orchestrator to decide and action separately.

The owner decision on sendBeacon / fetchLater (Pending Beacon) adoption to close the navigation-discard gap is pending and was explicitly out of scope per the diagnosis's `explicitlyNotProposed` list -- not evaluated or recommended here.
Why the same navigation-discard mechanism passed 4/4 in an earlier session is still not explained (per source diagnosis); this action did not re-investigate that question.
Single-player only, Chromium only -- no co-op, no journal authority flag, consistent with the source diagnosis's scope.
